Article Title: Wall Street jitters: Nasdaq retreats after Nvidia-fuelled rally; Anthropic slips below IPO price
Article Text:
The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO.

Anthropic falls below

IPO price

Nvidia, chip stocks retreat after rally

Investors await US inflation data, tariff developments

Dollar slips, bond yields steady

Wall Street retreated on Tuesday as technology stocks gave back some of the previous day's sharp gains, with investors booking profits and turning cautious ahead of key US inflation data. Nvidia and Anthropic led the decline in AI-linked stocks.The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the S&P 500 declined 0.50% to 7,201.09. However, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70.The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO. The rebound, however, failed to ease concerns over stretched AI valuations, rising infrastructure spending and the outlook for interest rates.Anthropic shares tumbled 6.5% to $81.90, slipping below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83, just days after the AI startup's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.The stock opened at $111.50 on November 19, with its fully diluted valuation briefly exceeding $2 trillion. However, it has since lost ground amid a broader technology selloff.Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its IPO after underwriters exercised their option to purchase additional shares, making it the biggest public offering on record and surpassing SpaceX's $85.7 billion listing in June.CEO Dario Amodei sold more than 3.37 million shares worth over $280 million a day after the IPO, according to a filing late on Monday.The company's rapid reversal has renewed concerns about elevated AI valuations and the massive investments being made in computing infrastructure, particularly as higher interest rates could increase financing costs, Reuters reported.Anthropic is not the first major technology company to fall below its IPO price soon after listing. SpaceX took about a month to slip below its offer price, while Facebook, now Meta Platforms, fell below its IPO price on its second trading day in 2012.Nvidia shares fell 5.9% as investors reassessed the implications of Jensen Huang's return as CEO and the political and governance risks surrounding the company.The chipmaker had surged nearly 30% on Monday after Huang's reinstatement, helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq post their biggest daily percentage gains since April 2025.Technology stocks led the declines on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 technology sector falling 2.8%. The semiconductor index dropped 7.9%, reflecting renewed selling in AI-linked companies.Before Monday's rally, AI stocks had struggled for weeks as investors questioned whether the sector's debt-fuelled spending on infrastructure would generate sufficient returns.Investors are also looking ahead to Wednesday's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation gauge watched by the Federal Reserve ahead of its December policy meeting.Persistent inflation has strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy. Fed funds futures traders were pricing in a 98% probability of a rate hike in December and a 66% chance of another increase in January, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said late on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point towards tighter monetary policy.Investors were also wary of potential new tariffs after Reuters reported, citing three people familiar with the matter, that the Trump administration was preparing to release findings of a probe into alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners. The findings are expected to pave the way for new import duties on a wide range of goods.The administration's tariffs have contributed to higher consumer prices in the US, adding to inflation concerns.The dollar fell 0.44% against a basket of major currencies, retreating from a 20-month high touched earlier in the session.The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes edged up 0.77 basis points to 4.928%, compared with 4.92% late on Monday.The gap between two-year and 10-year Treasury yields, a closely watched indicator of economic expectations, stood at 24.3 basis points.Gold futures fell 2.67% and silver futures dropped 5.75%, pressured by hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials and expectations of higher interest rates.Brent crude futures settled $2.03 higher, or 2.27%, at $91.40 a barrel after a volatile session, with fresh attacks reported on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the S&P 500 declined 0.50% to 7,201.09. The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO. The rebound failed to ease concerns over stretched AI valuations, rising infrastructure spending and the outlook for interest rates.

Article Title: Nvidia shares surge 35.5% as tech giant reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and president
Article Text:
Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO (file photo)

What Jensen Huang said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Shares of Nvidia soared in trade on Monday after the tech giant announced the return of Jensen Huang as the company’s chief executive officer (CEO) with immediate effect. The decision comes within days of the company asking Huang to leave.The company's stock price soared over 35% to $170 level. Earlier, the announcement triggered a sharp rally in the company's stock, which climbed more than 30% in premarket trading. The stock had recorded its steepest weekly fall since 2008 last week, after Huang’s removal from the CEO position unsettled investors and heightened worries about the future prospects of the AI sector.Jensen Huang’s unexpected return to the helm of Nvidia also triggered a broad rally in the US stock market. The S&P 500 surged 4.5% on Monday, clawing back nearly half of the steep losses it suffered last week, one of its worst performances since the 2008 financial crisis.Technology stocks linked to artificial intelligence led the gains, pushing the Nasdaq Composite up 6.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 1,117 points.Signs of a rebound had emerged even before Wall Street opened and Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement.Futures trading indicated that US stocks were poised to break a seven-session losing streak, with markets expected to open more than 2% higher.Meanwhile, European technology stocks also climbed 4.7% after Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO.The decision represents a big departure of course for Nvidia's board, which had ruled out Huang's reinstatement only days earlier.Huang stepped down on November 12 following disclosures about extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for China. Beijing has denied the allegation.Explaining its decision to reinstate Huang, the board said it was satisfied with his candour and leadership capabilities. It added that, after consulting senior US government officials, it had concluded that his return posed no national security risk.“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” chair of the board Harvey C. Jones said in a statement Monday.Huang transformed Nvidia from a company primarily known for designing chips for video games into the leading supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence. During his tenure, he also guided the company's chip development strategy, negotiated customer agreements and managed its relationships in Washington.In a statement, Huang said he was “honored” to be back at the company and would take on the responsibility “with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”He also expressed his gratitude to Jones, interim CEO Colette Kress, who will resume her position as CFO, and Nvidia’s executive staff for steering the company through the brief period of uncertainty.“I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang’s statement continued. “Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family.I can’t wait to get back to work.”Huang transformed Nvidia from a company primarily known for designing chips for video games into the leading supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence. During his tenure, he also guided the company's chip development strategy, negotiated customer agreements and managed its relationships in Washington.
Article Summary: The company's stock price soared over 35% to $170 level. The decision comes within days of the company asking Huang to leave. The S&P 500 surged 4.5% on Monday, clawing back nearly half of the steep losses it suffered last week.

Article Title: IT sector employees seek national AI layoff policy as automation threatens jobs; unions and experts want NASSCOM and government to set minimum severance, advance notice, redeployment and reskilling ru
Article Text:
NITES has approached government authorities over concerns about mass layoffs. (Image for representative purpose only)

Policy for AI layoffs

Need for reliable data

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Amid the ongoing job uncertainty with regards to adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), especially in the IT sector, workers are now seeking protection. India’s information technology industry needs a common policy for reporting job losses caused by artificial intelligence and protecting workers affected by automation.Employee representatives and workforce experts are seeking minimum standards for advance notice, severance pay, internal redeployment and reskilling, rather than leaving these decisions entirely to individual employers.Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) has approached government authorities over concerns about mass layoffs, forced resignations and unfair employment practices.It is now seeking a separate policy framework specifically addressing job losses linked to AI.The proposed framework would require companies to record and disclose the number of positions eliminated because of AI, employees shifted to different roles within the organisation and workers retrained for new jobs, according to an ET report.It would also establish minimum expectations for employers to explore internal transfers before making employees redundant, offer fair compensation and help those affected find alternative employment.Harpreet Singh Saluja, president of NITES said companies should be able to adopt new technologies but must also account for the impact on employees’ livelihoods. He said technological progress should not come at the cost of leaving workers without adequate support.Saluja told the financial daily that employees and the government should have access to clear information on the number of workers affected, the reasons for eliminating positions and the extent to which technology is directly replacing jobs.He said employers should make genuine efforts to retrain employees or move them into other positions within the organisation before eliminating roles because of AI or automation. Saluja also called for adequate advance notice, fair severance packages and the settlement of outstanding dues. Reskilling, he stressed, should provide employees with meaningful opportunities to take up new work, rather than being limited to a handful of online courses.TeamLease Digital estimates that over the next 18-24 months, 30% of jobs in the technology sector could face compression, while AI could significantly augment another 45% of roles. The remaining 25% could move towards higher-value work involving AI, data, cloud computing and cybersecurity.Employees are looking for exit packages similar to those provided by Microsoft and Canva. Under Microsoft's voluntary exit programme in India, eligible employees received one month's base salary for every completed year of service, along with health insurance and career transition assistance.Neeti Sharma, chief executive of staffing firm TeamLease Digital, told ET that the IT industry currently has no clearly defined, common policy setting minimum requirements for severance, redeployment or reskilling when employees lose their jobs because of AI.She called for baseline safeguards covering advance communication, fair exit compensation, opportunities to move into other roles within the company and employer-funded reskilling. Sharma also said companies should maintain data on positions eliminated due to AI, employees transferred internally and workers trained for different roles.Ravi Venkatesan, founder of the Institute for Human Flourishing (IHF), said the matter required a national-level response instead of separate approaches by individual companies. He suggested that an industry association such as NASSCOM should consult its members and prioritise disclosure of workforce reductions.Venkatesan said society needed reliable data and evidence on these developments to determine the appropriate policy response. He also called for a national safety net that defines employers’ responsibilities towards workers who lose their jobs and clarifies the government's role in helping them transition to new employment.He argued that fair severance should be governed by a national policy rather than left solely to individual company rules. He also stressed the need to establish what responsibilities employers and the government should share in helping displaced workers acquire the skills required for new jobs.Canva, which announced a restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, equivalent to 22% of its workforce, offered those leaving the company at least six months' salary, healthcare coverage where applicable and career support. The company maintained that the positions being eliminated were not being replaced by AI.ET had earlier reported that employees affected by Qualcomm's workforce reduction in India were offered two months' notice pay, an additional month's salary for every year of service, continued insurance coverage for a year, stock awards and placement assistance, among other benefits. These details were provided by employees familiar with the exit arrangements and were not publicly confirmed by the company.However, despite growing demands for common industry-wide safeguards, there is little indication that companies are jointly developing such a framework.Pareekh Jain, chief executive of EIIRTrend, said companies had not begun discussions on a common policy, even as employees were raising the issue. He said workers wanted fair exit packages comparable to those offered by Microsoft and Canva. Some were also approaching the government for tax relief on their final settlements.The absence of transparent data is another obstacle to determining the actual extent of AI-driven job losses, said Kamal Karanth, co-founder of Xpheno. He observed that the last period when the industry had some visibility into workforce reductions was during the pandemic-related layoffs between late 2020 and 2022.
Article Summary: Employee representatives and workforce experts are seeking minimum standards for advance notice, severance pay, internal redeployment and reskilling. NITES has approached government authorities over concerns about mass layoffs, forced resignations and unfair employment practices. It is now seeking a separate policy framework specifically addressing job losses linked to AI.

Article Title: US targeting India's manufacturing schemes while protecting its own industry through tariffs: GTRI
Article Text:
Representative image

GTRI calls excess capacity claims a pretext for trade deals

India says it has no structural excess capacity

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Labour-intensive exports among those at risk

The United States is questioning India's manufacturing support initiatives, including the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme and Make in India, even as it uses tariffs to protect its own manufacturing interests, Ajay Srivastava, founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), has said.His remarks come after the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, citing structural excess manufacturing capacity. The proposed rate could be 17% if a trade deal is signed.Speaking to news agency ANI, Srivastava said Washington was criticising India's manufacturing policies because they could make domestic production more competitive and reduce demand for American goods."For India also, they listed all the schemes which India is using, and they are saying they are all hurting US manufacturers. So anything good you are doing in your country is hurting US manufacturing because, if you are making things in your country, US goods will sell less," he said.Srivastava argued that India was not the only country facing such scrutiny, with the US action covering 16 economies, including the European Union and China."They are targeting 16 economies. When I say economies, they target the European Union also, which has 27 countries. So almost all the big trading partners of the US have been targeted with high tariffs," he said.Referring to Cambodia, he said the USTR had also criticised its economic policies, labour laws and efforts to promote manufacturing.Srivastava alleged that Washington was using concerns over excess manufacturing capacity to push countries towards trade agreements that favour the US."Excess capacities are just a pretence for an extractive one-sided trade deal," he said, arguing that the proposed tariffs were being used to pressure countries, including India, into signing trade agreements.He urged the Indian government to use the consultation period to present its case and explain why the country does not have structural excess capacity. According to Srivastava, the US has opened a window for consultations extending until January.He also asked India to highlight subsidies provided by the US to its agricultural sector while responding to the allegations."If you talk about agriculture, it is the US which subsidises its agriculture, so they have the most excess capacity. They have to look back into what they are doing also instead of accusing," he said.The Union commerce and industry ministry has said India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.The ministry said the USTR notice was under examination and that India had engaged constructively throughout the investigation."In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the department of commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector," the ministry said.The proposed tariffs follow an eight-month investigation under Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974, which examined alleged unfair trade practices involving 16 trading partners.India has also maintained that trade-related concerns should be addressed through the ongoing negotiations for the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA)."India and the United States are engaged in negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement. It has been India's position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations," the ministry said, reiterating the government's commitment to an early conclusion of the pact.Srivastava estimated that around 50-52% of India's exports to the US could be affected by the proposed tariffs. These include labour-intensive sectors such as textiles, leather, garments, handicrafts and some auto components.However, around 40% of India's exports, including diesel, petrol, generic medicines and iPhone-type products, would continue to enter the US at zero tariffs, he said.Steel, aluminium and copper, along with some auto components, would continue to face tariffs higher than 25%, currently at 50%. These products account for around 7-8% of India's exports to the US, according to Srivastava.The proposed tariffs cover economies including India, China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam, among others.
Article Summary: The United States has proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods. The proposed rate could be 17% if a trade deal is signed. Ajay Srivastava, founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), says the US is criticising India's manufacturing policies because they could make domestic production more competitive and reduce demand for American goods.

Article Title: Nvidia halts server shipments to 4 Southeast Asian countries amid chip scandal; China not on list: Report
Article Text:
Nvidia halts server shipments to 4 Southeast Asian countries amid US curbs.

Megaspeed under scrutiny over possible chip diversion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia has instructed its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its advanced chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported on Thursday, amid tighter US export controls aimed at preventing Chinese firms from accessing restricted artificial intelligence processors through overseas data centres.The reported halt covers the four Southeast Asian countries, while China is not among the destinations named in the report.According to the FT, manufacturing partners including Dell and Supermicro, which integrate Nvidia chips into servers, have informed buyers in the four countries that Nvidia would not permit their orders to be shipped.The move follows new US restrictions that came into effect last week and require export licences for shipments of advanced chips to several Southeast Asian countries. Washington is seeking to close potential routes through which Chinese companies are believed to be accessing advanced AI computing power.It remains unclear whether the shipment halt is temporary or will continue as Nvidia and its manufacturing partners work to meet the new compliance requirements, the FT reported, citing three people familiar with the matter.Nvidia, Dell and Supermicro did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours.The latest restrictions come amid increased scrutiny of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that rents computing capacity at its data centres.The company has come under scrutiny over possible illegal diversion of advanced AI chips to China, as US authorities seek to prevent Chinese firms from accessing restricted processors through data centres operating outside the country.The US Commerce Department introduced the new export control rule days after reports involving Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy who had previously worked at Megaspeed. Nvidia's board subsequently reinstated Huang as CEO on November 23.The developments have brought renewed attention to the role of overseas data centres in providing Chinese companies access to advanced computing infrastructure despite US restrictions on direct chip exports to China.
Article Summary: N Nvidia has instructed its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its advanced chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The move follows new US restrictions that came into effect last week and require export licences for shipments of advanced chips. Washington is seeking to close potential routes through which Chinese companies are believed to be accessing advanced AI computing power.

Bengaluru: Haldyn Glass is acquiring German glassmaker Heinz Glas International’s entire 43.2% stake in their joint venture, Haldyn Heinz Fine Glass (HHFG), for Rs 45.1 crore, making the premium glass packaging manufacturer a wholly owned subsidiary. Incorporated in 2015, HHFG was set up to cater to demand for premium small-format glass containers used in cosmetics, skincare, perfumery and home fragrance products. The joint venture combined Heinz Glas’s technical and product development expertise with Haldyn Glass’s manufacturing capabilities and presence in the Indian market.HHFG operates a 105-tonne-per-day manufacturing facility at Kosamba in Gujarat, with integrated decoration capabilities. It supplies American, European and Indian brands.Heinz Glas will continue to provide marketing support for HHFG’s sales commitments for another two years, ensuring continuity in its engagement with international customers, Haldyn Glass said.The acquisition is expected to give Haldyn greater control over HHFG’s operations and allow it to leverage the manufacturing capabilities of both facilities. The company expects the move to improve capacity utilisation, generate operational synergies and support earnings growth.It also expects the transaction to be earnings per share (EPS) accretive and improve its consolidated performance.The deal will strengthen Haldyn’s presence in higher-value glass packaging, particularly in the premium cosmetics and personal care segments, while giving it access to a wider international customer base.“We are pleased to announce the acquisition of Heinz Glas’s stake in HHFG, marking an important milestone in our growth journey,” said Tarun Shetty, managing director of Haldyn Glass. The decade-long partnership helped the company build capabilities in premium glass packaging and work with leading international brands, he said.Incorporated in 1991, Haldyn Glass manufactures containers for the food, pharmaceutical, beverage, liquor and beer industries. Its two glass melting furnaces have a combined capacity of 435 tonnes per day. The company operates nine IS machines and produces containers ranging from 60 ml to 1,750 ml.HHFG’s turnover rose to Rs 177.1 crore in FY26, from Rs 152.9 crore in FY25 and Rs 143.5 crore in FY24. It reported revenue from operations of Rs 123.18 crore in the first half of FY27, with an EBITDA of Rs 23.25 crore, translating into a 19% margin. Its net profit stood at Rs 6.6 crore.
Article Summary: Haldyn Glass is acquiring German glassmaker Heinz Glas International’s entire 43.2% stake in their joint venture, Haldyn Heinz Fine Glass (HHFG), for Rs 45.1 crore. HHFG was set up to cater to demand for premium small-format glass containers used in cosmetics, skincare, perfumery and home fragrance products.

Article Title: RBI continues to bring back gold to India as it repatriates 60 tonnes more of yellow metal, India now houses 84% of its 880.52 metric tonnes gold reserves while remaining are with Bank of England and
Article Text:
Global gold prices fell by around 9%, with the average price dropping from $4,721 per troy ounce in April 2026 to $4,319 in September. (Image for representative purpose only)

RBI moves back most of India’s gold reserves

India’s forex reserves

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has been bringing back India’s gold stored abroad for some time now and it continued to shift the yellow metal reserves back even in this year.However, what is interesting to note is that gold accounted for a smaller proportion of the country's overall foreign exchange reserves at the end of September, data released on Wednesday showed.Despite the increase in gold held within India, its share in total foreign exchange reserves fell to 14.38% at the end of September, compared with 16.7% six months earlier.According to the RBI's latest half-yearly report, India's gold reserves stood at 880.52 metric tonnes at the end of September. Of this, 740.13 metric tonnes, equivalent to 84% of the total, were held within the country.The remaining 140.39 metric tonnes were kept with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements.RBI repatriated around 60 tonnes of gold during April-September 2026. India has been progressively repatriating its gold holdings over the past two years amid rising geopolitical risks. In March, 77% of the country's gold reserves were held domestically.India's foreign exchange reserves totalled $705.3 billion, according to the latest data released by the central bank on Friday.When reserves stood at $668.6 billion at the end of June, they were sufficient to cover 9.8 months of imports, the RBI said.The ratio of short-term debt to foreign exchange reserves climbed to 23% at the end of June 2026, up from 21.6% at the end of March. The ratio of volatile capital flows, including portfolio investments, to reserves also increased, reaching 68% at the end of June against 66.6% three months earlier.Most of India's foreign exchange reserves continue to be invested in securities issued by overseas governments. In addition, $35.95 billion was held as deposits with other central banks and the Bank for International Settlements, while $42.75 billion was deposited with commercial banks abroad."With the objective of exploring new strategies and products in reserve management while diversifying the portfolio, a small portion of the reserves is being managed by external asset managers," the RBI said.The period was marked by heightened geopolitical uncertainty, driven by the conflict in West Asia, interruptions to energy supplies and tighter monetary policies adopted by several major central banks.Global gold prices fell by around 9%, with the average price dropping from $4,721 per troy ounce in April 2026 to $4,319 in September."Prices responded to rising US Treasury yields, a stronger US dollar and expectations of tighter monetary policy. The decline occurred despite continued investor demand for gold as a safe-haven and for portfolio diversification," the report noted.India's overall foreign exchange reserves, meanwhile, grew by $46.67 billion during April-September 2026. They increased from $691.11 billion at the end of March to $737.78 billion at the end of September.Of the $608.26 billion in foreign currency assets held at the end of September, $529.57 billion was invested in securities. A further $35.95 billion was placed with other central banks and the BIS, while $42.75 billion was maintained as deposits with commercial banks overseas.The report also pointed to shifts in the composition of global foreign exchange reserves. The US dollar's share fell from 57.18% in the first quarter of 2026 to 56.70% in the second quarter. Over the same period, the euro's share rose from 20.04% to 20.60%.The RBI reiterated that protecting the safety of India's foreign exchange reserves and ensuring their liquidity remain the central priorities in managing the portfolio, with returns optimised within these parameters.
Article Summary: India's gold reserves stood at 880.52 metric tonnes at the end of September. Of this, 740.13 metric tonnes, equivalent to 84% of the total, were held within the country. The remaining 140.39 metric tonnes were kept with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements.

Article Title: Travel pushes LRS remittances past $3bn in September

MUMBAI: Outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) rose 15% month-on-month to a 24-month high of $3.2 billion in Sept, from $2.7 billion in Aug, driven largely by higher spending on overseas travel. Remittances for travel increased 21% to almost $2 billion from $1.6 billion, accounting for nearly 84% of the overall increase in outward remittances during the month.The remittances had last crossed $3 billion in Aug 2024. Transfers as gifts increased 15% to $247 million, while remittances for maintaining close relatives overseas rose 13% to $311 million. Remittances for medical treatment also declined to $3.7 million from $4.8 million. Overall, the Sept increase was primarily travel-led, with higher overseas investment, gifts and family maintenance transfers providing additional support.
Article Summary: Remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) rose 15% month-on- month to a 24-month high of $3.2 billion in Sept. Remittances for travel increased 21% to almost $2 billion from $1.6 billion, accounting for nearly 84% of the overall increase in outward remittances.

Article Title: Abrupt end to Kalyan-raj at Flipkart
Article Text:
Krishnamurthy’s association with Flipkart goes back nearly 15 years, when he left eBay to join Tiger Global, a key investor in the company. He served as Flipkart’s interim CFO in 2013-14 before returning to Tiger.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Flipkart group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy, who helped turn around the homegrown e-commerce major when it was losing ground to Amazon, is leaving after nearly a decade at the helm, amid differences with parent Walmart over listing plans and financial priorities.Krishnamurthy’s last working day will be Dec 4, just nine days after the announcement, according to an internal communication from Walmart International president and CEO Chris Nicholas to employees, reviewed by TOI. An emergency town hall was called on Wednesday, with the news of an abrupt leadership transition at one of India’s most valuable internet companies catching even senior leadership off guard.“Most of us were clueless. It’s so sudden since tension, if any, was not apparent,” a senior Flipkart executive told TOI.Sources in the know claimed Krishnamurthy and Walmart’s leadership differed over the timing of Flipkart’s public listing and providing liquidity to employees holding stock options. While an initial public offering ( IPO ) had been in the works for some time, Walmart has been pushing the company to improve its financial performance before going public.Chief product and technology officer Balaji Thiagarajan and the Flipkart board will lead the company in the interim.A successor will be announced in the coming weeks.Krishnamurthy’s association with Flipkart goes back nearly 15 years, when he left eBay to join Tiger Global, a key investor in the company. He served as Flipkart’s interim CFO in 2013-14 before returning to Tiger.His return in mid-2016 came during the most difficult period in Flipkart’s history. Sales growth had stagnated, repeated valuation markdowns hurt investor sentiment, senior executives were leaving and Amazon had committed $5 billion to India.Focusing on smartphones, large appliances and branded fashion, Krishnamurthy helped Flipkart regain market share, demonstrating an Indian startup could hold its own against a global giant. Co-founder Binny Bansal had replaced Sachin Bansal as CEO in 2016.
Article Summary: Krishnamurthy’s association with Flipkart goes back nearly 15 years, when he left eBay to join Tiger Global, a key investor in the company. An emergency town hall was called on Wednesday, with the news of an abrupt leadership transition catching even senior leadership off guard. A successor will be announced in the coming weeks.

Article Title: Lakshmi Venu moves Madras high court for partition of family assets

Lakshmi Venu’s claim is based on her interpretation of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, which recognises daughters’ rights in coparcenary property.

CHENNAI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan, has filed a suit before Madras HC seeking partition of the joint family assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family and allotment of her share in them, claiming efforts to reach an amicable settlement have failed.The suit follows a partition notice she sent to her father, Venu Srinivasan, on Nov 16, asking him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and ensure a fair and lawful division of the assets.Venu Srinivasan’s response reflected no change in his position, according to a statement issued on her behalf. Lakshmi has also sought the court’s intervention to obtain documents and information that she alleges have been withheld despite repeated requests.Lakshmi compelled to approach court: MallikaThe suit concerns the ownership and division of joint family assets and does not seek to interfere with the operations of any company, the statement said. Lakshmi has an interest in the continued strength of the businesses and believes any division of assets can be implemented in an orderly manner in accordance with the law.Supporting her claim, her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, said Lakshmi had been compelled to approach the court after the response to her notice failed to recognise her rights and no progress has been made towards amicable resolution.“As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect,” she said.Lakshmi Venu’s claim is based on her interpretation of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, which recognises daughters’ rights in coparcenary property. The assets she seeks to partition include interests held through the VS Trust and other holding entities in businesses such as TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton, allocated to the Venu Srinivasan branch under the 2020 TVS Group family arrangement.She contends the arrangement did not constitute a partition within her immediate family and that no division or settlement of its assets has been initiated or concluded.
Article Summary: Lakshmi Venu seeks partition of the joint family assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family. She claims efforts to reach an amicable settlement have failed. Her claim is based on her interpretation of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005.

Article Title: Fresh 25% Trump tariff threat with a carrot of 17% duty: What it means for India
Article Text:
The Trump administration has announced that the tariffs on India could range from 17-25% depending on the finalisation of a trade deal between the two countries.

What has the Donald Trump administration announced? Why has India been selected among the list of countries subject to fresh tariffs? And what does it mean for trade deal talks and India’s export prospects?

What Trump administration has announced

Trump's new tariff threat against India

Why these tariffs on India?

Industrial plans aimed at expanding manufacturing Insufficient labour protections Policies involving financial repression Persistent barriers to market access; and Failure to tackle global excess capacity and production, including through imports and foreign direct investment from non-market economies.

Tariff Threat: Key Allegations by US Against India

What it means for India and trade deal talks with US

How India's Tariffs Compare to others

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Amid the India-US trade deal negotiations, the Donald Trump administration unveiled a fresh set of tariffs aimed at a host of countries including India.The proposed tariffs, for which several countries have been targeted, form a part of the United States Trade Representative's (USTR) Section 301 investigations into structural excess capacity.China faces the hardest hit with a potential final tariff rate of up to 45% for some of its goods.In India’s case the tariffs could go up to as high as 25%. The twist is the prospect of lower tariffs if a trade deal is finalised.The Trump administration has announced that the tariffs on India could range from 17-25% depending on the finalisation of a trade deal between the two countries.Up to 25% tariffs on all goods from India, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods would be applicable, but there is also the prospect of 17% tariffs if a trade deal is agreed on.“The Trade Representative further proposes to consider whether the additional duties applied should be adjusted to account for, among others, duties applied under other, existing Section 301 actions; duties applied under other, existing Section 232 actions, or were India to reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the United States that is responsive to the determinations in this investigation into the acts, policies, and practices of India, a tariff rate of 17 percent,” the USTR release reads.It’s also important to note that the new tariffs will not be levied on top of any existing tariffs that are applicable to specific sectors.For many months now, the USTR's office has been examining whether 16 countries follow policies that encourage excess capacity production. Such practices can push prices down and undermine US industries, according to the investigation.Interestingly, the probe came on the back of the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn the Trump administration's reciprocal tariffs and was widely seen as an alternative way for the government to keep the tariff pressure on the country’s trading partners.Following the US apex court ruling, the USTR had launched two investigations under Section 301. While one covered about a hundred countries, over alleged violations of export regulations relating to forced labour, the other targeted 16 economies over policies aimed at encouraging excess production.Because the US claims that it has found India among many countries indulging in what it claims are unreasonable acts, policies and practices. The US has identified five areas that it sees as practices that end up being detrimental to US interests:According to the assessment, these acts, policies and practices place a burden on or restrict US commerce in three ways. They limit business opportunities for US producers and exporters in India and other countries; damage the US economy by contributing to declines in domestic manufacturing output, exports, employment and investment; and heighten economic security risks for the US, including through dependence on inputs from non-market economies.According to the Trump administration, these concerns are particularly significant in sectors such as healthcare, including pharmaceuticals and medical devices, as well as steel, solar energy and information and communications technology (ICT).The step assumes significance because the India-US trade deal is yet to be finalised. Despite repeated statements from both sides on talks being in final stages, no deal has yet been announced. In February this year, the US announced an 18% tariff on India after imposing 50% duties in August 2025. However, with the US Supreme Court ruling that reciprocal tariffs are illegal, India continued to face low tariffs like all other countries.India has time and again said that a trade deal will be finalised once it gets a favourable tariff rate compared to its competitors. Now, with the US adding pressure of up to 25% tariffs in the absence of a trade deal, it remains to be seen whether talks will be expedited.Manoj Mishra, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader, Grant Thornton Bharat believes that the proposed US tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, net of existing Section 301 tariffs and subject to certain exemptions, could pose fresh challenges for Indian exporters.“The USTR’s scrutiny of India’s Make in India, PLI and Atmanirbhar Bharat initiatives, particularly in the steel, solar, pharmaceuticals and electronics sectors, has wider implications for India’s manufacturing ambitions,” he tells TOI.According to Mishra, the proposed tariffs could increase landed costs, erode export competitiveness, compress margins and impact manufacturing investments.But, what does it mean for trade deal talks?“The possibility of a lower tariff rate of 17%, contingent upon India concluding an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the US that addresses the investigation findings, underscores the need to expedite bilateral trade negotiations,” Mishra says.“To mitigate the impact, India could leverage its expanding network of FTAs, explore alternative export markets and diversify global supply chains to reduce dependence on the US market,” he adds.Ajay Srivastava, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) points out that under the proposal, India’s exports get a calculated 1% edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18% deal rate) and a 3% edge over Vietnam and China (20% deal rate).“By deploying a dual-rate structure - threatening steep baseline tariffs against countries that refuse a pact while offering lower rates to those that sign - Washington reclaims the bargaining power to impose duties at will and extract unilateral concessions, allowing a government to secure tariff relief even if the industrial capacity that prompted the investigation remains unchanged,” he opines.“Because these manipulated rates are a deliberate bait to extract one-sided concessions - and with the threat of Graham tariffs of up to 100% still hanging over it - India must reject the trade deal and instead answer the allegations sector by sector, showing that its investment serves domestic buyers, overseas customers, and future demand rather than letting exports alone be treated as proof of excess capacity,” Srivastava says.Agneshwar Sen, Trade Policy Leader, EY India believes that the proposed tariffs reinforce the broader shift towards a more protectionist global trade environment.“For India, the key priority will be to preserve competitiveness and market access in the US while continuing to diversify export markets and strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities,” he tells TOI.
Article Summary: The Trump administration has announced that the tariffs on India could range from 17-25% depending on the finalisation of a trade deal between the two countries. The proposed tariffs form a part of the United States Trade Representative's (USTR) Section 301 investigations into structural excess capacity.

Article Title: Another Nvidia romance draws scrutiny: Jay Puri's ties to executive at a firm linked to China
Article Text:
Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia sales chief, and former Super Micro executive Cenly Chen's marriage draws scrutiny amid a US probe into alleged chip smuggling to China (Image credit: Clash Report's X)

How their professional roles overlapped

Super Micro's China-linked chip probe

How the relationship came under scrutiny

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia executive who led its global sales team, is facing scrutiny over his relationship with Cenly Chen, a former senior executive at US-based server maker Super Micro Computer. The couple dated for several years and married on March 7 this year, according to records. Their relationship has come under the spotlight amid a US investigation into allegations that Super Micro servers loaded with Nvidia chips were diverted to China.Chen was Super Micro's chief growth officer and regularly dealt with Puri when the company was seeking access to Nvidia's chips for its customers, according to current and former employees of both companies, The Wall Street Journal reported.She also accompanied Super Micro CEO Charles Liang on visits to Nvidia's offices, where he pressed the chipmaker to supply products to the company's customers.During Super Micro sales meetings, Chen encouraged employees to approach her with questions related to Nvidia, positioning herself as the company's key contact on such matters, employees said.Puri, meanwhile, headed Nvidia's global sales team, which was responsible for deciding how the company's latest chips were allocated among customers.He joined Nvidia in 2005 after spending two decades at Sun Microsystems and working at other technology companies. He stepped back from his global sales role in July but remained a senior adviser.Chen denied that her relationship with Puri influenced her professional decisions. “I never had to rely on personal relationships for professional gain,” she said in an email as quoted in the WSJ report.She also said she was not involved in selecting or procuring chips for Super Micro. “I dealt with Super Micro’s customers and the customer decided the chips they bought,” Chen said, adding, “I was not involved in the selection or procurement of the chips.”Super Micro said Chen “did not manage Supermicro’s overall relationship with Nvidia or our procurement of Nvidia GPUs. Our relationship with Nvidia spans dozens of teams, functions and projects.” The company added that allocation of Nvidia chips to its customers was determined through a multi-department process.The scrutiny comes as Super Micro faces a US investigation into an alleged scheme to divert servers containing high-end Nvidia chips to China.On March 19, the US justice department unsealed charges against Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, a sales manager and a third-party broker. The indictment accused the three of conspiring to smuggle more than $500 million worth of servers containing Nvidia chips into China.Prosecutors alleged that the accused directed an unidentified company in Southeast Asia to place orders worth around $2.5 billion for Super Micro servers in 2024 and 2025, before diverting at least $510 million worth of equipment to China.Super Micro was not named as a defendant and has said it was a victim of the alleged scheme. Chen was not named in the indictment and said she had not been contacted by federal law enforcement. The company said it was cooperating with authorities and had cut ties with the individuals charged.Liaw has pleaded not guilty and resigned from Super Micro's board in March. The third-party broker has pleaded guilty under an agreement with prosecutors.Chen's relationship with Puri came under renewed attention after a shareholder lawsuit alleged that she played a role in Super Micro's acquisition of Nvidia chips. Short seller Muddy Waters also highlighted the couple's ties in a research report earlier this month.Chen spent nearly two decades at Super Micro after joining the San Jose-based company in 2008. She later became its chief growth officer, overseeing the sales team dealing with some of its biggest customers. She left the company after Nvidia's annual conference in March and was named CEO of cloud services company ChronoScale, which was spun out of Applied Digital, another Nvidia partner.Wes Cummins, CEO of Applied Digital and chairman of ChronoScale, said Chen had helped Applied Digital establish its cloud business and had advocated with Nvidia on behalf of customers. He acknowledged that her relationship with Puri created the appearance of a conflict of interest, but said he was unaware of Super Micro receiving any special treatment from Nvidia.Cummins also said the relationship had prevented ChronoScale and Applied Digital from accessing some Nvidia assistance available to customers because of the disclosed conflict of interest.Puri and Chen's relationship was known to people who worked with them. They were photographed together at the San Francisco Opera's annual masked gala in September 2024 and later attended a California Academy of Sciences gala in April with other Nvidia executives and their spouses.The developments come amid scrutiny of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's personal and professional relationships with executives at companies linked to allegations of chip diversion to China.Huang had an extramarital relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed International, another Nvidia customer. Some US officials suspect Alice Huang of having worked with Chinese intelligence.Both Megaspeed and Super Micro are dealing with justice department investigations into allegations of chip smuggling to China.
Article Summary: Jay Puri, a longtime Nvidia sales chief, and former Super Micro executive Cenly Chen's marriage draws scrutiny. Their relationship has come under the spotlight amid a US investigation into allegations that Super Micro servers loaded with Nvidia chips were diverted to China. Puri and Chen dated for several years and married on March 7 this year.

Article Title: 44 Nvidia trades put Trump’s financial interests under spotlight after CEO’s return
Article Text:
File photo: US president Donald Trump and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

US president Donald Trump ’s investment portfolios traded shares of chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times between January and September, with the value of his holdings potentially rising by as much as $15 million after the company’s stock surged following the return of chief executive Jensen Huang.A review of Trump’s financial disclosures by BBC Verify found that his portfolios bought between $5.2 million and $17 million worth of Nvidia shares during the first nine months of the year, while selling between $4.4 million and $12 million worth.The filings, submitted to the US Office of Government Ethics, report transactions in broad value ranges rather than exact amounts, making it impossible to establish precisely how much Nvidia stock Trump traded or how many shares he held.Trump’s latest disclosure, submitted on November 5, indicated that he could have held as many as 370,000 Nvidia shares as of September 30.Nvidia shares surged more than 30% on Monday after the company’s board reinstated Huang as CEO, potentially increasing the value of Trump’s investment by $15 million.The rally followed Trump’s public involvement in Huang’s reinstatement. The president told CNBC he had spoken to Nvidia’s board and “made the deal” to bring the executive back.Nvidia said it had received input from senior US government officials before deciding Huang’s return posed no national security risk.Trump’s portfolios also held between $12.5 million and $58 million worth of Nvidia shares at the end of 2025, according to the disclosures.The White House has said Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third parties, and that neither the president nor his family can direct or influence investment decisions.The frequent trading of Nvidia shares has nevertheless raised questions about potential conflicts of interest, particularly given Trump’s role in the company’s leadership decision and the administration’s oversight of advanced chip exports to China.Nvidia has become one of the world’s most valuable companies amid the boom in artificial intelligence. Its shares account for more than 6% of the S&P 500, making it one of the most influential stocks in the index.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump traded shares of chipmaker Nvidia at least 44 times between January and September. The value of his holdings could rise by as much as $15 million after the company’s stock surged following the return of chief executive Jensen Huang.

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorised Elon Musk 's SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites that will function as data centres in space, as the company seeks to meet rapidly growing demand for artificial intelligence computing.The FCC said on Wednesday it had approved SpaceX's proposed "Starmind" constellation of orbital computing modules which would process massive amounts of data and transmit it back to Earth.SpaceX had earlier sought permission to deploy up to 1 million satellites to support AI computing infrastructure in space.The FCC said the approval would allow SpaceX "to pioneer emergent technology that advances American leadership in space and artificial intelligence".Data centres are the physical backbone of artificial intelligence, requiring enormous amounts of electricity to run and cool computing systems.SpaceX has proposed powering its orbital data centres using solar energy, arguing that the technology could significantly reduce energy costs and the environmental impact associated with conventional data centres on Earth."By directly harnessing near-constant solar power with little operating or maintenance costs, these satellites will achieve transformative cost and energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centers," SpaceX told the FCC.The company plans to use its next-generation Starship rocket which is currently under development to deploy the constellation.The ambitious proposal depends heavily on Starship's ability to lower launch costs and carry large numbers of satellites into orbit.FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the approval would help the US strengthen its position in artificial intelligence and expand computing infrastructure."America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence. Under President Trump's leadership, the United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people. The FCC supercharges that effort today by granting, for the first time ever, authorization to deploy 1 million orbital compute modules for data centers in space. This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth," Carr said."Compute campuses or data centers are essential to sustaining America’s leadership in SI. By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centers are meeting the moment. This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," he added.The FCC has also approved SpaceX's request to establish backup communications for its optical network. The system will use radiofrequency links for emergency telemetry, tracking and command operations, as well as backup connectivity across the satellite network.The approval allows communications in the 18.8–19.3 GHz bands for downlinks and 28.6–29.1 GHz bands for uplinks.It remains unclear whether SpaceX will eventually deploy the entire constellation. There are currently around 17,000 satellites in orbit, and deploying 1 million would represent an unprecedented expansion of satellite infrastructure, Reuters reported.Satellite operators often seek approval for larger constellations than they ultimately intend to deploy, allowing flexibility as their technology and business plans evolve.SpaceX had previously sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites. The network currently has more than 11,000 satellites in orbit.Amazon's satellite unit Leo and other competitors have questioned SpaceX's proposed constellation arguing that deploying the entire network could take centuries and that the company may not launch all the satellites it has sought approval for.Carr dismissed the criticism in March, saying, "Amazon should focus on getting Amazon's house in order with their own launches and their own satellite constellation, rather than worrying about other people that are actually out there ​launching satellites at the pace and cadence that SpaceX is."Under the approval, SpaceX must begin deployment by November 2033 and launch at least 10% of the approved constellation, or 100,000 satellites by November 2035 and deploy 50% by November 2038.
Article Summary: SpaceX had earlier sought permission to deploy up to 1 million satellites to support AI computing infrastructure in space. The company plans to use its next- generation Starship rocket which is currently under development to deploy the constellation. SpaceX must begin deployment by November 2033 and launch at least 10% of the approved constellation.

Article Title: US GDP growth revised sharply higher to 4.3% in third quarter on strong consumer spending, AI investment
Article Text:
US economy expands at 4.3% annualised rate in Q3, nearly double Q2 growth (representative image)

Domestic demand remains strong

Corporate profits rise at slower pace

Inflation remains a concern

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The US economy grew at a faster-than-expected annualised rate of 4.3% in the July-September quarter of 2026, significantly higher than the earlier estimate of 3.4%, as stronger consumer spending and business investment supported economic activity.The revised estimate, released by the commerce department's Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on Wednesday, marked the fastest pace of growth in three years. Economists polled by Reuters had expected the figure to be revised up to 3.5%.The economy had expanded at an annualised rate of 2.2% in the April-June quarter, meaning growth nearly doubled in the third quarter.The upward revision reflected stronger-than-previously estimated consumer spending and investment. The BEA said real GDP was revised up by 0.9 percentage point from its advance estimate, primarily due to upward revisions in these two components.Consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the US economy, rose at a revised rate of 4.2%, compared with the earlier estimate of 3.8%.Business investment also remained strong. Spending on equipment increased at an annualised rate of 21.8%, up from the previously estimated 20.9%.According to Reuters, business investment has recorded double-digit growth for three consecutive quarters, although economists have warned that this pace could slow as investors scrutinise valuations of artificial intelligence companies.The BEA said the acceleration in economic growth compared with the second quarter primarily reflected stronger investment and an upturn in government spending, partly offset by a decline in exports.Imports also increased during the quarter, according to the BEA data.A key measure of domestic demand, real final sales to private domestic purchasers, which excludes inventories, trade and government spending, rose at an annualised rate of 5.8%.This was the fastest increase since the second quarter of 2021 and higher than the earlier estimate of 4.9%.The upward revision in investment was led primarily by intellectual property products, particularly software, while stronger consumer spending reflected increased expenditure on goods, including pharmaceuticals, computer software and accessories, and petrol and other energy products.Higher-income households were driving much of the consumer spending, supported by gains in stock market wealth before the recent AI-led sell-off.Historically low layoffs and moderate hiring have also helped other households sustain expenditure, although wage growth has at times lagged inflation. Households have also been saving less and drawing on their accumulated savings.Despite the stronger economic expansion, the increase in corporate profits moderated during the quarter.Profits from current production rose by $206 billion in the July-September period, compared with an increase of $384 billion in the preceding quarter, the BEA said.The income-side measure of economic activity also showed strong growth. Gross domestic income (GDI) increased at an annualised rate of 4.4% in the third quarter, compared with a 2.3% rise in the second quarter.The average of GDP and GDI, which is considered a broader measure of economic activity, also grew at a rate of 4.4%.The revised GDP figures came alongside fresh inflation data that showed continued price pressures in the US economy.The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.8% year-on-year in October, matching a three-year high recorded in May.The increase was accompanied by higher energy prices and a rise in non-durable goods inflation. The PCE inflation rate remained well above the Federal Reserve's long-term target of 2%, which it has missed for almost six years.The quarterly PCE price index rose by 2.1%, while core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, stood at 2.5%, according to the BEA figures.The Federal Reserve had held interest rates steady at its October meeting after raising them in September. With inflation continuing to run above its target, the possibility of another rate increase at its December meeting remained in focus.The strong growth figures underline the resilience of the US economy despite headwinds, including President Donald Trump's tariff policies and higher energy prices linked to the war on Iran.The AI investment boom has also supported economic activity, while economists have pointed to a widening gap between higher- and lower-income households in their ability to sustain spending.
Article Summary: US economy expands at 4.3% annualised rate in Q3, nearly double Q2 growth.Domestic demand remains strong but corporate profits rise at slower pace. Inflation remains a concern as Federal Reserve continues to focus on interest rates.

Article Title: US proposes new tariffs on India, 13 other trade partners; China faces additional 20% duty
Article Text:
No tariffs are proposed on goods from Mexico and Norway for now (File photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With ANI inputs)

The Donald Trump administration on Wednesday proposed fresh tariffs on 14 of Washington's major trading partners, including India, citing concerns over "excess industrial capacity" and its adverse impact on US commerce, Reuters reported.The proposed measures follow an eight-month investigation conducted by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) under Section 301, which examined alleged unfair trade practices involving 16 trading partners.The countries and trading blocs targeted by the proposed tariffs include China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.However, Mexico and Norway have been left out of the proposed measures for now.A senior US official told Reuters that Washington had determined that these countries "create, sustain, or contribute to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors" through policies and practices considered "unreasonable' and "harmful" to US commerce.India and Vietnam, in particular, are among the countries that have yet to conclude trade agreements with the US.China is expected to face the highest cumulative tariff burden. The proposed 20% duties would come in addition to tariffs of around 25% imposed during Trump's first presidential term.However, the new duties would not be levied over the 10% or 12.5% tariffs introduced in July over allegations that certain countries had failed to adequately enforce anti-forced labour laws.Beijing, however, has rejected the allegations, arguing that its exports are driven by the country's competitive advantages, Reuters reported.Meanwhile, the US official also said the proposed measures would adhere to tariff limits established under existing trade agreements. These include a 15% ceiling for the European Union, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, and a 19% limit for Malaysia.Specific tariff rates for each trading partner were expected to be outlined in a notice to be published in the US Federal Register on Wednesday.Before the measures can take effect, they will be subject to a public notice-and-comment process and a hearing. According to the official, implementation could be pushed back to January 2027.The Trump administration has repeatedly accused China of flooding international markets with manufactured goods, including steel, aluminium, electric vehicles and solar products, by maintaining excess production capacity.
Article Summary: The Donald Trump administration on Wednesday proposed fresh tariffs on 14 of Washington's major trading partners, including India. The proposed measures follow an eight-month investigation conducted by the Office of the United States Trade Representative. The countries and trading blocs targeted by the proposed tariffs include China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.

Article Title: Trump set to hit India, China, 14 others with new tariffs after probe
Article Text:
After the set​back in the US SC over the use of emergency powers to impose "reciprocal tariffs", the Trump admins had launched two probes under Section 301.​

Section 301 probe : Govt doesn’t expect any negative impact

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Eight months after it launched a probe on alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 countries, including India, China and the European Union, the US Trade Representative is all set to unveil its findings in the case and propose tariffs.The Wall Street Journal said the US is preparing to raise tariffs this week, with Bloomberg reporting that it may come in as early as Tuesday. Indian officials are keeping a close watch on the outcome of the probe, which is likely to be followed by a set of hearings, before final tariffs are announced, in around 45 days.After the setback in the US Supreme Court over the use of emergency powers to impose "reciprocal tariffs", the Trump administration had launched two probes under Section 301.While additional tariffs of 10-12.5 per cent were imposed on imports from over 50 countries, including India, for their alleged failure to prohibit the import of goods with forced labour, which harmed American exports, the outcome of the second investigation is awaited.Going by the mood here, the government does not expect any negative impact, although it maintains that there is no structural excess capacity in India and the surplus is in anticipation of higher demand in the world’s fastest-growing major economy.In fact, during deliberations with the US government too, officials have made it clear that the government has not provided subsidy or other support to create capacity, while underlining that any country which has surplus domestic production is engaged in exports.The report by USTR will be followed by hearings before the final tariff is announced. In the first probe, India had managed to get concessions with the final levy of 10 per cent imposed, against 12.5 per cent, proposed initially. The outcome of the investigation will provide clarity on Trump’s new tariff framework, although the final levy will be known in around 45 days. Based on the final tariff, governments will engage in negotiations for “trade deals”. India is confident of negotiating a deal where its exports enjoy “comparative advantage” over rivals from the region.While the first set of tariffs related to forced labour have been challenged in US courts, even the second one is expected to face litigation, especially because USTR findings are similar for almost all countries. In the case of structural excess capacity, among the top 20 trading partners for the US, all except Canada, the UK, Brazil and Australia are facing action, with the large European countries being part of the EU. The list also includes Norway, Indonesia, Cambodia and Bangladesh, which are not among the top 20 partners for goods and services trade.
Article Summary: The Wall Street Journal said the US is preparing to raise tariffs this week. Indian officials are keeping a close watch on the outcome of the probe. The report by USTR will be followed by hearings before the final tariff is announced. The outcome of investigation will provide clarity on Trump’s new tariff framework.

Article Title: A low-Huanging fruit? Jensen burner may have netted Trump a $15 million windfall
Article Text:
Trump's intervention to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have boosted the value of his stock holdings by up to $15 million

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump has never been shy about claiming credit for a good deal. His latest presidential intervention, however, may have delivered a whopping personal windfall: by some estimates as much as $15 million in gains on his Nvidia stock after he persuaded the company to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang.Nvidia shares surged 31.5 per cent on Monday, adding nearly $1 trillion to the company's market value after its board reversed Huang's departure, barely 11 days after he resigned following an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese spy agencies. An analysis of Trump's latest financial disclosures by the Financial Times estimated that his Nvidia holdings could have appreciated by between $1.3 million and $15 million in Monday's rally alone.The wide range reflects the imprecise nature of the disclosures, which report transactions in dollar bands rather than exact share counts. Depending on the assumptions about purchases and sales, Trump may have held anywhere between 32,000 and 370,000 shares as of September 30. His latest disclosure, filed on November 5, records several Nvidia purchases in September, including transactions in a range reaching $250,000.Crucially, it does not cover October or November, leaving unanswered the question of whether he bought or sold shares during the period immediately preceding Huang's reinstatement.The $15 million, therefore, is a potential paper gain, not a realised profit. Nor does it establish that Trump traded on inside information. But the coincidence is remarkable enough to invite questions about the intersection of presidential influence and personal financial interests, an issue Democrats -- some of whom are also accused of being on the make -- are ready to get their teeth into.Trump himself was candid about his role in the corporate resurrection. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he told CNBC on Monday. "And I convinced them ... I made the deal." The MAGA boss was not merely cheering from the sidelines either. According to reports, veep JD Vance, himself a former Silicon Valley venture capitalist, also intervened over the weekend, acting as an emissary to Nvidia's boardThe board eventually capitulated, saying it had received assurances from senior US government officials that Huang's return did not pose a national security risk. Trump himself virtually absolved Alice Huang of being an intelligence operative despite leaks from the US intel about her ties to Chinese agencies, saying any beautiful woman who comes from China is usually dubbed a spy.The White House's defence about alleged Trump profiteering is that his portfolio is managed by independent third-party financial institutions, which make investment decisions without his involvement and replicate broad market indices such as the Schwab 1000. The administration has also described his assets as being held in a trust managed by his children, although the precise management arrangements have not always been explained consistently.Experts say all this does not eliminate the underlying conflict: a president can influence the fortunes of companies in which his family-controlled financial arrangements have significant exposure. Besides, Nvidia is hardly an isolated case, although the President's broader financial portfolio makes the Nvidia episode particularly striking. Trump's latest annual disclosure, covering 2025, showed that he received more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency ventures, including World Liberty Financial, the family-backed crypto business liked to Pakistan, and his $TRUMP meme coin. The proceeds have helped swell his conventional stock and bond portfolio to an estimated $703 million to $2.6 billion by the end of last year, according to a Reuters analysis.The growing perception among critics is that the Trump family and its business associates are making off like bandits while the President presides over decisions that can move markets and determine corporate fortunes. The concern is not necessarily that every transaction is improper, but that the administration has blurred the boundary between public authority and private enrichment to an extent rarely seen in modern American politics.The Nvidia affair is particularly striking because it follows Trump's extraordinary intervention at Intel last year. After publicly questioning the national security credentials of Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan and demanding his removal over his past China connections, Trump changed course following a White House meeting. The eventual arrangement gave the US government a 10 per cent non-voting stake in the struggling chipmaker, converting $11.1 billion in government grants and commitments into shares.Trump himself described the deal as something he had personally negotiated. The government became one of Intel's largest shareholders, while Tan retained his job. Nvidia now presents an even more unusual variation of the same phenomenon. Washington does not own a stake in the company, as it does in Intel. But its influence over Nvidia's leadership, export permissions and national security standing has become unmistakable. The company has effectively discovered that its boardroom decisions can require presidential blessing.The Wall Street Journal, among others, has described Nvidia as having become, in effect, a government-backed enterprise. Huang owes his reinstatement to Trump, and the company's ability to navigate its continuing legal and regulatory troubles may depend considerably on the administration's goodwill.Meanwhile, Congress, which is itself far from being a paragon of virtue, is up in arms. Raja Krishnamoorthi, the Illinois Democrat who chairs the House Select Committee on China, called Huang's reinstatement "outrageous," arguing that neither the government nor Nvidia's board had completed its investigation into what information Chinese intelligence might have obtained. He has demanded a full public congressional hearing, insisting that the American people deserve answers.Even Republicans are asking uncomfortable questions. Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, always ready with colorful observations, said it was not his business to police Huang's marital conduct while calling it “the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy.” But a relationship with someone potentially connected to Chinese intelligence was an entirely different matter because it jeopardizes national security, he said, adding that he wanted officials to explain whether export controls had been circumvented.He also called for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to answer questions under oath about the handling of the suspected chip-diversion affair.The controversy is gradually feeding into a wider Washington debate about the extraordinary monetisation of political access, a debate complicated by the fact that lawmakers from both sides have been accused of minting money with insider info. Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi has faced years of scrutiny over the spectacular investment returns associated with trades made by her husband, venture capitalist Paul Pelosi.
Article Summary: Trump's intervention to reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have boosted the value of his stock holdings by up to $15 million. Trump himself was candid about his role in the corporate resurrection. "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," he told CNBC on Monday.
